Saber programação não é exigência mas será um diferencial.
summary:
CerradoShift is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform developed to help farmers adapt crop rotation strategies to changing environmental conditions. Focused on Brazil's Cerrado biome, the project integrates NASA Earth observation data with climate information, soil characteristics, vegetation monitoring, and scientific agricultural models.

The platform allows users to explore regional environmental conditions, assess soil and water-related risks, and compare crop rotation strategies through an accessible interactive interface.

By combining NASA POWER climate data, satellite-based vegetation indicators, and complementary geospatial datasets, CerradoShift transforms complex environmental information into understandable insights for agricultural planning.

Our goal is to make scientific data more accessible, support climate-resilient farming decisions, and encourage sustainable land management. The platform is designed as a preliminary decision-support tool rather than a replacement for laboratory soil analysis or professional agronomic recommendations.
details:
How Does CerradoShift Work?

CerradoShift connects environmental data acquisition, geospatial processing, scientific analysis, and interactive visualization into a unified agricultural decision-support platform.

Users can select an agricultural location, explore climate and soil-related indicators, monitor vegetation conditions, and assess potential crop rotation strategies.

The backend, developed with Python and FastAPI, integrates NASA POWER, satellite-derived vegetation information, Open-Meteo, and complementary geospatial datasets. Scientific models process available environmental variables to identify climate-related risks, water limitations, and relevant soil conditions.

The frontend, developed using React and Vite, presents these results through an accessible web interface.

What Makes CerradoShift Different?

Rather than displaying satellite data without context, CerradoShift connects environmental observations to agricultural planning decisions.

The platform emphasizes:

  • Environmental integration: Combining climate, soil, and vegetation information.
  • Scientific transparency: Distinguishing measured data, model estimates, and missing information.
  • Regional relevance: Focusing on the agricultural challenges of Brazil's Cerrado.
  • Accessible technology: Delivering scientific insights through an interactive web application.
  • Sustainability: Supporting crop rotation planning and climate adaptation.

Technologies Used

Frontend: React, JavaScript, Vite

Backend: Python, FastAPI

Scientific and geospatial tools: Rasterio, NumPy, Google Earth Engine integration, and custom agricultural models

Environmental data: NASA POWER, NASA HLS, ISRIC SoilGrids, MapBiomas, Open-Meteo, and regional Brazilian datasets.

Expected Impact

CerradoShift aims to support more informed crop rotation planning, improve awareness of environmental constraints, and make satellite-based scientific information easier to interpret.

The project demonstrates how open Earth observation data can be transformed into practical tools for agricultural sustainability, particularly in regions exposed to climate variability and water-related risks.

Some datasets require external configuration, and results depend on data availability. The platform is intended to support preliminary assessments and does not replace professional agronomic recommendations.
